evidence: Tier 1 (executed differential, oracle-generated): the unmodified product-sdk libOpenMS (Debug, core 4fdec46; git diff 4fdec46..bc9cc12 empty for IMDataConverter.{h,cpp}, IMDataConverter_test.cpp, FAIMSHelper.cpp, MSExperiment.{h,cpp}, LogStream.{h,cpp}, MzMLHandler.cpp, ExperimentalSettings.cpp, SpectrumRangeManager.h and MSSpectrum.cpp; installed IMDataConverter.h and FAIMSHelper.h equal to the pin) executed splitByFAIMSCV on six mzML files and 20 synthetic experiments. For every file the Rust reader produces the C++ native IDs, MS levels, drift time bits and units, and for every case without a NaN voltage the Rust split produces the C++ group count, group keys bit for bit (sign of zero and infinities included), group sizes, group membership and order by native ID, MS level, drift time bits and unit, settings copies (date, comment, sqMass run id, equality with the input), chromatogram counts, the emptied input, and the log lines (compared through an emulation of the C++ log stream's repetition cache). The C2 records (both synthetic FAIMS fixtures and the FFC_1 input under the source sequence, and facts 1a and 1b) are reproduced: -45 with 112 spectra; -60 and -45 with 56 each; NaN with 112; -60 and -45 with 2 each. The three NaN cases are refused natively, with the input unchanged, and their recorded C++ outcomes are asserted. Tier 3: the three splitByFAIMSCV sections and the constructor and destructor sections of IMDataConverter_test.cpp are transcribed unchanged. Tier 4: the group key, the message records, the returned skipped spectra and chromatograms, atomicity on error, the settings resource ceiling and MAX_SPECTRA. Native difference, not emulated: C++ voltage groups have no ranges (byMSLevel(1) throws, recorded for every voltage group); Rust ranges are computed on demand and present. No Debug-only precondition lies on this path.
